correctness.rationale: Every group of originally identical 3-bit column types evolves identically; the update is exactly a row sum less the local bit plus the two vertical bits. The eight-profile reduction and multinomial weight recover all labelled configurations. Two fully specified unbounded QF_LIA negations of the claimed iterate identities were checked unsatisfiable against libz3, yielding F^5=F^3 for all odd widths >=3 and F^6=F^4 for all even widths >=2. The parameterized 3-group trajectories realize 3 and 4 steps in the stated ranges. All 299,584 configurations for widths 2..6 were independently evolved at vertex level and matched to the profile census; the small even cases were exhaustive. Limit: solver soundness is trusted; no hand-written independent refutation of the SMT queries exists.

evidence: The classic Goles-Olivos period-two theorem gives eventual least period at most 2 on finite symmetric threshold networks, but no specific uniform cutoff of 3/4 for L(K_{3,n}).

Benjamini et al., arXiv:1405.2486, introduction Section 1 and Sections 2-3, deal with infinite unimodular and random graphs; Kaaser et al., arXiv:1508.03519, Sections 1 and 3 analyze general O(|E|) and module-sensitive bounds.
broader_coverage.reasoning: General eventual period two is strictly weaker than a sharp uniform first-entry time, and broad general bounds do not provide the exact parity threshold or every layer count. The present proof separately establishes its strong identity F^5=F^3 (odd) or F^6=F^4 (even) and its sharpness.

originality.rationale: Closest general primary results establish eventual 2-periodicity, worst-time bounds or random-graph behavior but not the sharp three-row parity law. The accessible earlier two-row matched-clique claim has different adjacency and does not imply the three-row law. A finite 4x4 rook-graph table cannot determine the 3xn family or unbounded witnesses. Originality is best-knowledge conditional on inspected sources, not historical certification.

value.rationale: The natural connected, increasing-degree graph L(K_{3,n}) has a sharp size-independent relaxation bound with a genuine parity split: all odd widths have largest first-entry time 3, whereas every even width >=6 has an explicit 4-step witness. The exact eight-type multinomial formula partitions all 2^(3n) labelled configurations by first entry and least period at polynomial profile cost. This reveals a nontrivial dynamical boundary not supplied by the general finite-graph period-two theorem.
